titre: CAN 2025 : le Sénégal récupère le titre, le Maroc dénonce un incident, la décision finale du TAS et les recours
resume: La décision du Tribunal Arbitral du Sport est attendue dans la journée pour déterminer le vainqueur entre le Maroc et le Sénégal.
texte:
La décision du Tribunal Arbitral du Sport a redonné la victoire au Sénégal face au Maroc après la finale controversée de 2025.
Le Tribunal Arbitral du Sport s'est réuni au début du mois d'octobre à Lausanne pour auditionner le dossier opposant le Sénégal au Maroc et à la Confédération Africaine de Football. Ce litige concerne la finale chaotique de la CAN 2025, disputée le 18 janvier à Rabat. Un petit rappel des faits... Lors de la finale entre le Maroc et le Sénégal, plusieurs joueurs sénégalais avaient quitté temporairement la pelouse pour protester contre un penalty accordé au Maroc après un but refusé au Sénégal. Après 15 minutes de confusion et des débordements dans les tribunes, Brahim Diaz avait manqué ce penalty litigieux. Pape Gueye avait ensuite offert la victoire au Sénégal en marquant durant la prolongation.
En mars dernier, le jury d'appel de la CAF avait décidé de retirer le titre de champion au Sénégal et de le déclarer forfait, en vertu des articles 82 et 84 du règlement de la compétition. Le résultat avait alors été homologué sur le score de 3-0 en faveur du Maroc. C'est cette décision que la Fédération Sénégalaise conteste devant le TAS. Le Français Gérald Simon a présidé les débats, assisté des Professeurs Luigi Fumagalli et Ulrich Haas.
Finalement, ce mardi 24 novembre, le Tribunal Arbitral du Sport a livré son verdict à l'unanimité après la finale controversée de la CAN 2025. L’instance a officiellement désigné le Sénégal comme vainqueur de la compétition. Pour rappel, le Maroc peut encore faire appel de cette décision devant le Tribunal Fédéral Suisse, qui juge plus la forme que le fond du dossier. Un peu plus tôt dans la journée, le Maroc avait dénoncé un incident. D'après RMC, le conseil juridique de la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football a adressé un courrier officiel au Tribunal Arbitral du Sport afin de signaler "un incident" qui serait survenu ces dernières heures. Selon la partie marocaine, une communication téléphonique aurait eu lieu dimanche entre le juriste allemand, l'un des trois arbitres désignés par le TAS pour statuer sur l’affaire de la finale de la CAN, et Abdoulaye Fall, président de la Fédération Sénégalaise de Football. Dans ce signalement, la partie marocaine indique qu’elle se réserve le droit d'engager des recours. Le Sénégal rejette cette information.
Dans un communiqué de presse, la Fédération marocaine a exprimé "sa protestation face au fait que sa demande n’ait pas été prise en considération. Celle-ci portait sur les conséquences juridiques à tirer des pratiques ayant entaché la procédure et remettant en cause l’intégrité et la crédibilité de la décision, notamment après qu’il a été confirmé qu’un contact avait eu lieu entre l’arbitre allemand, Ulrich Haas, et le président de la Fédération sénégalaise de football, 48 heures avant le prononcé de la décision. En conséquence, la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Football a décidé d’engager toutes les procédures légales nécessaires afin de contester la décision du TAS", écrit-elle dans un communiqué.
Le délai est désormais de 30 jours à compter de la notification de la décision pour faire appel devant cette instance. Saisir le Tribunal fédéral n’est possible que pour des motifs bien précis et au nombre de cinq :
Cet appel devant le Tribunal fédéral suisse constitue l’ultime recours dans le cadre de ce dossier opposant le Sénégal à la CAF et à la Fédération royale marocaine.
"Après ces longs mois d’attente, c’est avant tout un immense soulagement, mais aussi une grande fierté de voir cette deuxième étoile revenir au Sénégal", a commenté sur Instagram Pape Gueye, qui promet au peuple sénégalais que l'équipe nationale fera "toujours le maximum pour vous rendre fiers". Le buteur du sacre sénégalais n'en oublie toutefois pas les "frères marocains". "Au-delà du football, le respect et la fraternité entre nos deux peuples restent les plus importants. Gardons ça. Au final, c’est l’Afrique qui gagne."
La décision du TAS sur la CAN 2025 a forcément un impact sur le classement Fifa. Alors que le Maroc était à la 5e place quand la Fifa comptabilisait la finale de la CAN 2025 comme une victoire par forfait 3-0 du Maroc, en revenant à 1-0 pour le Sénégal, le Maroc perd 18 points et recule dans le même temps de deux places, soit en 7e position. Le Portugal et le Brésil repassent quant à eux devant. En revanche, le Sénégal se maintient à la 18e place.
What the CAS ruling does to the FIFA ranking? Senegal are African champions again: CAS restored their 1-0 win over Morocco in the AFCON 2025 final. FIFA has scored that final as a 3-0 forfeit win for Morocco since its April ranking. If it switches back to the 1-0: Morocco -18.0, down 2 to 7th, 1.0 point above Belgium Portugal and Brazil up 1 to 5th and 6th Senegal +22.0, still 18th, 7.3 points behind Japan If FIFA re-runs every match since January instead, it is about +17.9 and -13.9, with the same places. on the card = places moved from the official ranking of 18 November
Le footballeur sénégalais Sadio Mané n'a pas manqué de réagir à la décision du TAS concernant la CAN 2025, "qui rétablit le Sénégal dans son titre de champion d’Afrique". Une décision qui "nous remplit de joie", a-t-il sobrement déclaré, avant de remercier les Sénégalais et ses coéquipiers. "Je veux d’abord dire merci à tout le peuple sénégalais, au pays comme dans la diaspora. Vous nous avez soutenus du premier match jusqu’à cette décision. Votre confiance nous a donné de la force dans les moments les plus difficiles", a-t-il déclaré, ajoutant : "Merci à mes coéquipiers. Je sais les efforts et les sacrifices que chacun a consentis pour cette deuxième étoile." Sadio Mané s'est également dit "fier d'avoir vécu cette aventure" à leurs côtés. Surtout, Sadio Mané a adressé un "message de respect et d’encouragement au peuple marocain et aux joueurs du Maroc", estimant qu'"ils ont réalisé un beau parcours et peuvent en être fiers". Et d'ajouter : "Je leur souhaite le meilleur pour la suite."
Ismai

En choisissant de rendre au Sénégal son titre de la CAN-2025, obtenu sur le terrain mais perdu au profit du Maroc sur tapis vert dans un premier temps, "le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) a rendu justice au sport", s'est félicité, mardi 24 novembre, le président de la fédération sénégalaise de football, Abdoulaye Fall. Le correspondant de Radio France internationale à Dakar rapporte qu'il n'y a pas de fête organisée dans la capitale. "Nous avons toujours considéré que nous avions gagné. Il ne restait qu’à officialiser cette victoire. Nous n’attendions que ça", explique un supporter à RFI.

titre: AFCON 2025: Abdoulaye Fall savors Senegal's victory before the CAS and dedicates the second star to Aïda Faye Samb
resume: Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) decision in favor of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) in its dispute with CAF and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, Abdoulaye Fall ...
texte:
CAN-2025 : Abdoulaye Fall savoure la victoire du Sénégal devant le TAS et dédie la deuxième étoile à Aïda Faye Samb
Following the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) decision in favor of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) in its dispute with CAF and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, Abdoulaye Fall hailed it as a "victory for sports law." The FSF president paid tribute to the Lions and dedicated their second continental title to Aïda Faye Samb, the supporter who died while traveling to Morocco to support the Lions.
The CAS decision was met with profound relief by the president of the FSF. In his address to the sporting nation, Abdoulaye Fall spoke of a "controlled joy" and a "legitimate pride," while emphasizing the legal and sporting significance of this decision.
“Following a thorough examination of the facts and the law, the CAS arbitration panel upheld our appeal. It overturned decision DC23316 issued on March 17, 2026, by the CAF Appeals Board, dismissed the administrative forfeit (3-0) that had been awarded against our national team, and fully reinstated, in legal and sporting terms, the victory achieved and confirmed on the field on January 18, 2026, at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Complex in Rabat (Senegal 1-0 Morocco, after extra time). The second continental star won by our Lions of Teranga is thus definitively confirmed,” explains Abdoulaye Fall.
For him, "this verdict is not revenge on either side. It consecrates the triumph of sports law, independent international arbitration, and the universal primacy of the truth on the pitch."
He recalls that the FSF had chosen not to appeal the initial decision of the CAF Disciplinary Committee, preferring to accept the financial penalties imposed. However, following the reversal of the appeals committee's decision on March 17, the federation decided to take the matter to the international arbitration tribunal.
He thus paid a heartfelt tribute to those who had achieved victory, praising the players who represented the national team throughout the competition. He specifically honored captain Kalidou Koulibaly, Sadio Mané, voted best player of the tournament, Édouard Mendy, and Pape Guèye, who scored the winning goal in the final.
He also expressed his gratitude to former coach Pape Bouna Thiaw, the entire technical, medical, and administrative staff, as well as the team of lawyers led by Seydou Diagne. He also commended the international counsel who defended Senegal's interests before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).
The FSF president also expressed his gratitude to the President of the Republic, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, the Prime Minister and the entire government for their support, while emphasizing respect for the statutory autonomy of the federation.
His thoughts also go out to Aïda Faye Samb, the young Senegalese supporter who lost her life while traveling to Morocco to support the Lions. "This second star, now legally sealed, is dedicated to her enduring memory," writes Abdoulaye Fall, who also includes in this tribute the 18 grieving Senegalese supporters who suffered in the aftermath of the final.
Beyond the satisfaction stemming from the CAS decision, Abdoulaye Fall calls for turning the page on tensions between Dakar and Rabat. He extends fraternal greetings to the Moroccan national team, its federation, and the Moroccan people, recalling the historical and religious ties between the two countries.
He also praised CAF President Patrice Motsepe for his commitment to respecting and implementing the arbitration ruling.
The head of Senegalese football now intends to work with CAF to finalize the administrative, regulatory, and financial formalities stemming from the decision. He also advocates for a modernization of the statutes, arbitration, and jurisdictional bodies of the continental governing body.
Finally, Abdoulaye Fall invites the Senegalese to look ahead to the next events, particularly the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, with coach Patrick Vieira and the Lions.
For him, this legal victory must go beyond the simple framework of a confrontation between two federations. "The greatness of a victory is measured by its capacity to unite and build," he says, calling for fair play, exemplary conduct, and African fraternity to prevail.

titre: Senegal–Morocco: CAS restores Senegal as 2025 African champions
resume: Ten months after a final that deeply divided African football, Senegal are officially the 2025 African champions. On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the Court of Ar ...
texte:
Ten months after a final that deeply divided African football, Senegal are officially the 2025 African champions. On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of the Senegalese Football Federation, overturning the Confederation of African Football’s decision that had awarded the title to Morocco by administrative ruling. The Lions of Teranga have therefore been officially restored as champions and retain the trophy they won on the pitch in Rabat.
It is the dramatic conclusion to a case that had overshadowed African football since January.
By overturning the decision issued by CAF’s Appeal Jury on March 17, 2026, CAS restored the sporting result of the final: a 1-0 victory for Senegal after extra time.
The Lausanne-based tribunal therefore rejected the regulatory interpretation that had led to Senegal being sanctioned with a forfeiture defeat.
Senegal won the final against Morocco thanks to a goal from Pape Gueye in extra time.
But several minutes earlier, the match had descended into an extremely tense situation.
Deep into stoppage time, referee Jean-Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR intervention.
Angered by the decision, Senegal head coach Pape Thiaw instructed his players to temporarily leave the pitch.
Led notably by Sadio Mané, the Senegalese players eventually returned to the field.
Brahim Diaz then missed Morocco’s penalty before Pape Gueye scored the decisive goal in extra time.
The Royal Moroccan Football Federation quickly challenged the way the match had unfolded.
After its initial complaint was rejected by the disciplinary committee, CAF’s Appeal Jury ultimately ruled in Morocco’s favour on March 17.
Relying notably on Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, the body declared Senegal to have lost the match by forfeiture and awarded Morocco an administrative 3-0 victory.
The Senegalese Football Federation immediately challenged that decision.
On March 25, the FSF formally appealed to CAS, seeking to have CAF’s ruling overturned and the result achieved on the pitch officially reinstated.
A closed-door hearing was subsequently held on October 8 in Lausanne.
Several weeks of deliberation were ultimately required before the decision was delivered on Tuesday, November 24.
With this ruling, Senegal officially regain their status as 2025 African champions.
The national team therefore adds a second Africa Cup of Nations title to its honours list, following its first triumph in 2022 in Cameroon.
For Pape Thiaw’s side, the title won on the pitch is now also recognised legally.
For Morocco, however, the verdict represents a major setback.
As host nation, the Kingdom had hoped to secure a second continental crown, fifty years after its first title in 1976.
CAS’s decision ultimately confirms the result achieved on the field and leaves Morocco with one African title in their history.
A few hours before the decision was announced, the FRMF reported an incident relating to the proceedings.
According to RMC Sport, the Moroccan side referred to an alleged telephone conversation that may have taken place on Sunday between Ulrich Haas, one of the arbitrators appointed to hear the case, and Abdoulaye Fall, president of the Senegalese Football Federation.
Morocco reportedly wanted clarification over the exact content of that alleged exchange.
If a procedural irregularity were eventually established, the FRMF could potentially explore further legal options, particularly on procedural grounds before the Swiss Federal Supreme Court.
However, one important point remains: CAS stated a few hours before delivering its verdict that it had not received the report announced by the Moroccan side.
At this stage, no conclusion can therefore be drawn regarding the possible consequences of this new controversy.
On the substance of the case, the CAS ruling brings the main dispute to an end: Senegal are officially recognised as the winners of the 2025 AFCON.
After ten months of legal proceedings, appeals and controversy, the Lions of Teranga have regained the title they won on the pitch in Rabat.
One final question nevertheless remains: will the Lausanne ruling truly bring this saga to an end, or could the incident reported by Morocco open a new legal chapter?
Toute l'actualité du football africain et européen : mercato, résultats et classements.

titre: 2025 AFCON Final: Why the CAS overturned the CAF decision and reinstated Senegal as African champions
resume: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favor of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in the dispute concerning the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations ...
texte:
Finale CAN 2025: Pourquoi le TAS a annulé la décision de la CAF et rétabli le Sénégal dans son titre de champion d’Afrique
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favor of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, in the dispute concerning the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. By overturning the decision of the Appeals Committee of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), which had declared Senegal a forfeit and awarded the victory to Morocco with a score of 3-0, the sports court reinstated the result obtained on the field with a Senegalese victory (1-0).
The legal saga surrounding the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final has reached a decisive turning point. Following the controversial decision of March 17, 2026, the Swiss Football Federation (FSF) seized the matter and the Lausanne-based arbitration body examined the circumstances of the match, the arguments of the various parties, and the application of CAF regulations.
At the heart of this case, a fundamental question remains: could a match played to its conclusion, and then won by a team, be transformed into a defeat by forfeit following a decision taken after the match?
Among the reasons cited were irregularities in the procedure followed by the CAF bodies. The CAS considers that the contested decision was affected by procedural flaws significant enough to justify its annulment.
The other determining factor concerns respect for the principles of natural justice.
These principles notably require respect for the adversarial process, the right for each party to present its observations and arguments, as well as the requirement of a fair and impartial procedure.
Their violation constitutes an infringement of the fundamental guarantees that must govern all disciplinary or judicial proceedings. In this case, this aspect calls into question the legality of the decision taken by the CAF Appeals Board.
Beyond procedural issues, the sporting outcome of the match occupies a central place in the dispute.
On January 18, 2026, in Rabat, Senegal beat Morocco 1-0, in a final marked by strong tensions after a penalty was awarded to the Moroccans and the ensuing Senegalese protest.
The decision of the CAF Appeals Jury, issued on March 17, then overturned the result of the match by declaring Senegal forfeit and ratifying a 3-0 victory for Morocco.
By overturning this decision, the CAS reinstates the original result of the final. Senegal is thus recognized as the winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.
The implications of the ruling are considerable. It renders ineffective the decision of the CAF Appeals Board, which had stripped Senegal of its victory and awarded the title to Morocco.
This is therefore not simply a recommendation addressed to the African body, but an arbitral decision that settles the dispute submitted to its examination.
The 1-0 result in favor of Senegal is reinstated and the Senegalese Football Federation regains the status of African champion federation 2025.
The execution of this decision now implies an update of the official acts and documents of the competition.
Three elements are particularly concerned: The trophy ( the official recognition of Senegal as the winner of the 2025 AFCON), the medals ( the regularization of their allocation in view of the restored result), The official ranking ( the correction of the registers and the list of winners of the competition).
The CAF will therefore have to draw the institutional and sporting consequences of the arbitration ruling.

titre: AFCON 2025: CAF accepts CAS ruling and confirms Senegal as champions
resume: The Confederation of African Football quickly reacted to the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling in the dispute between Senegal and Morocco over the 2025 AF ...
texte:
The Confederation of African Football quickly reacted to the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s ruling in the dispute between Senegal and Morocco over the 2025 AFCON final. Just hours after the decision was published, the continental body announced that it would fully respect the verdict delivered in Lausanne and take all necessary steps to implement it.
The long-running legal saga surrounding the 2025 AFCON final has therefore taken another major turn.
On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled in favour of the Senegalese Football Federation by overturning the decision issued by CAF’s Appeal Jury on March 17.
That ruling had declared Senegal to have lost the match by forfeiture and awarded Morocco an administrative 3-0 victory.
CAS ultimately reinstated the Lions of Teranga as winners of the competition.
In a statement released just hours after the verdict, the Confederation of African Football acknowledged the decision without announcing any intention to challenge it.
“CAF respects the CAS award and will take all necessary measures to implement it.”
The continental body also clearly confirmed the sporting consequences of the ruling:
“Senegal has therefore been declared by CAS as the winner of the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025.”
CAF has therefore officially recognised Senegal as the 2025 African champions.
This position is fully in line with the repeated statements made by Patrice Motsepe in recent months.
The CAF president had consistently insisted that the organisation would respect the Court of Arbitration for Sport’s decision, whatever the outcome.
As recently as Monday, on the eve of the ruling, Motsepe reiterated that position:
“Whatever decision comes out of CAS, we will respect it and comply with it.”
CAF’s reaction on Tuesday therefore confirms that the organisation intends to implement the Lausanne ruling.
While CAS overturned the decision that had stripped Senegal of the title, it upheld the ruling issued by CAF’s Disciplinary Board on February 11, 2026.
Several individual sanctions imposed following the incidents in the final therefore remain valid, although most have already been served.
Senegal head coach Pape Thiaw had been suspended for five matches and fined $100,000.
Ismaïla Sarr and Iliman Ndiaye were each handed two-match suspensions.
On the Moroccan side, Achraf Hakimi was given a two-match suspension, with one of those matches suspended for one year.
Ismaël Saibari was suspended for three matches and fined $100,000.
Financial penalties had also been imposed on both federations.
Senegal are officially recognised as the winners of the 2025 AFCON, while CAF has confirmed that it will fully implement the CAS decision.
After months of legal proceedings, appeals and controversy, the Lions of Teranga have therefore officially regained the crown they won on the pitch.
The remaining question is whether this ruling will finally bring the case to an end, with the Moroccan federation having already announced its intention to explore further legal avenues.

titre: Le Sénégal vainqueur de la CAN 2025 face au Maroc : « Le football a gagné », estime El-Hadji Diouf
